audit.whatIsWrong: Galio wins 65.52% of 29 games here — his best number in the slice — and the page labels it diff 'EVEN', tone yellow, difficulty 6/10, report[14] 'Even matchup'. The stage chart is worse: Skill, Warwick, Warwick, Skill, Skill, Warwick, Warwick, four rows to Warwick, while the content says 'This is your phase', 'Lane stays yours', and gives Galio five of seven rows in its own why-lines.
audit.why: This is the one matchup on the list a Galio should walk into confident, and every label tells him it is a coin flip he might lose. The prose and the win rate already agree with each other; only the labels dissent.

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl is never mentioned anywhere in either layer. Not in the ability list, not in the trade advice, not in the don'ts.
audit.why: It is the ability that beats Galio's whole plan. Primal Howl gives Warwick 2.5 seconds of damage reduction and then fears nearby enemies for 1 second — a fear is cast-inhibiting crowd control, so it breaks the Shield of Durand channel before the taunt ever releases. The entry tells you six times to 'taunt-release Shield of Durand' into his step-in and never mentions the 15-second button that cancels it.
audit.corrected: Primal Howl is 15s at rank 1: 2.5 seconds of damage reduction that ends in a 1-second fear. Do not start the W channel while it is up — bait it, then charge.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (E Primal Howl: 'gains damage reduction for 2.5 seconds. At the end, or if re-activated, he howls, causing nearby enemies to flee for 1 second', cooldown 15/14/13/12/11, flags hardCC)
champ-data/_kits/galio.json (W Shield of Durand: charged stance, taunt on release)

audit.whatIsWrong: The highest-value interaction in _missing-interactions.json for this pairing is absent: 'Your Justice Punch (E) shuts off Warwick's Jaws of the Beast (Q), Infinite Duress (R) — hold it for the engage, not the poke.'
audit.why: Both of Warwick's committal abilities are dashes, and Infinite Duress is additionally a channel that has to stay attached to its target for 1.5 seconds. Justice Punch is a knockup, so it is the answer to both — and the entry instead tells you to spend E as the second half of your own combo ('taunt-release, then chain E Justice Punch knockup'), which means it is never available when his R comes.
audit.corrected: Hold Justice Punch for his commit, not for your combo: the knockup answers both Jaws of the Beast and the Infinite Duress channel, and nothing else in your kit does.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (Q flags dash; R flags dash,hardCC,heal,channel)
champ-data/_kits/galio.json (E Justice Punch: 'knocking up the first enemy champion he encounters')

audit.whatIsWrong: early says 'your W's damage reduction is weak against his AD', wants.foe[1] says 'his AD shrugs off your magic-tuned Shield of Durand', late says 'your magic-resist W does little against his AD', and the full tldr opens 'Respect the physical damage'.
audit.why: Eternal Hunger adds bonus MAGIC damage to every one of Warwick's basic attacks, and it is the source of his early damage and his sub-50% healing. Shield of Durand cuts magic 25/30/35/40/45% against physical's 12.5/15/17.5/20/22.5%, so a meaningful slice of his auto damage is exactly what the stance is best at. Four separate lines tell the player his one defensive button is useless when it is partly the reason he wins the lane.
audit.corrected: Eternal Hunger is bonus magic damage on every auto, and Shield of Durand cuts magic at double the rate it cuts physical — the stance is doing real work here, on top of the taunt.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (P Eternal Hunger: 'basic attacks deal bonus magic damage')

audit.whatIsWrong: Every cooldown reference is 'when Infinite Duress is down' with no numbers, in tldr, winCon, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0], report[5] and report[9].
audit.why: Infinite Duress is 110/90/70 and Blood Hunt is 80/70/60/50/40 — both long enough to plan a whole wave around. Primal Howl at 15s and Jaws of the Beast at 8s are the two that actually govern a lane trade, and neither appears. The 'his R is down, go' advice is right; it just needs the clock.
audit.corrected: Infinite Duress 110s at rank 1; Blood Hunt 80s at rank 1; Primal Howl 15s; Jaws of the Beast 8s. Trade on Primal Howl's 15 seconds, all-in on the R's 110.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[2].why says 'the dash is interruptible and root-able mid-flight'.
audit.why: Justice Punch cannot be interrupted once travelling, and Warwick has no root — his crowd control is a 1-second fear on Primal Howl and a 1.5-second suppression on Infinite Duress. The fear does matter, but it matters during the W channel, not against the E in flight.
audit.corrected: Warwick has no root. What can stop your combo is Primal Howl's fear landing on the Shield of Durand channel — the charge itself cannot be interrupted mid-flight.
sources: wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Galio (Justice Punch cannot be interrupted mid-travel)
champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (E fear 1s; R suppress 1.5s; no root)

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions Grievous Wounds, and neither layer notes that Jaws of the Beast is percent-max-health.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags both needs-antiheal (Eternal Hunger, Jaws of the Beast, Infinite Duress) and resistances-invalidated (Jaws of the Beast) for this pairing. Jaws of the Beast damages 'based on their maximum health' and heals him for what it deals, so building health without anti-heal actively feeds him. The full layer has 'Oblivion Orb early'; the content page a player reads has nothing.
audit.corrected: Jaws of the Beast scales off your maximum health and heals him for the damage, so stacking HP without Grievous Wounds pays for his sustain.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (Q: 'dealing damage based on their maximum health and healing for damage dealt', flags dash,heal,percentHealth)

audit.why: Blood Hunt is 4000 range and reveals enemies below 50% health map-wide, and the entry's jungle line already tells you to ping when his R is down. Worth knowing that a low-HP Galio is visible to Warwick from anywhere on the map, but the existing advice — recall rather than linger low — is implied by wants.foe[0] and I did not need to add a negative line to state it.

edits.before: This is your phase. Your Q shove keeps him from free-stacking Q heals off the wave, and at 6 Hero's Entrance is a brutal all-in on a champion whose only mobility is his own R — flag, drop on him, taunt-knockup, and your follow-up deletes him before sustain matters. Just respect his R: if Infinite Duress lands while you're isolated it suppresses you straight out of your own taunt window, and his W speed means he picks the engage. Keep W and E up to peel his step-ins and force fights while his R is on cooldown.

Your Q shove keeps him from free-stacking Q heals off the wave, and at 6 Hero's Entrance is a brutal all-in on a champion whose only mobility is his own R — flag, drop on him, taunt-knockup, and your follow-up deletes him before sustain matters. Just respect Infinite Duress: 110 seconds at rank 1 and a 1.5-second suppress, but it is a channel, so hold Justice Punch and the knockup breaks it off you. Keep Primal Howl baited before every W channel and force fights while his R is down.

edits.before: Lane stays yours, but a fed Warwick reclaims relevance in teamfights — his R is a guaranteed lockdown on your carry and his drain scales with bruiser items, so the 2+ item window trends even. Your value here isn't the 1v1; it's R-presence and turning his engage against him — taunt him mid-leap to peel Infinite Duress off your carry, body-block the suppress, and use Hero's Entrance to flank fights across the map. Don't get caught alone late: an isolated extended fight where your magic-resist W does little against his AD is the one place he reliably beats you.
edits.after: Lane stays yours, but a fed Warwick reclaims relevance in teamfights — his R is a guaranteed 1.5-second lockdown on your carry and Jaws of the Beast scales off maximum health, so the 2+ item window trends even. Your value here isn't the 1v1; it's R-presence and turning his engage against him — Infinite Duress is a channel, so a Justice Punch knockup peels it straight off your carry, and Hero's Entrance flanks fights across the map. Buy Grievous Wounds early: his Q heals him for the damage it deals, so stacking health without it just pays for his sustain.

notes: Primal Howl was completely absent from both layers before this pass and is the ability that decides the lane, because a fear is cast-inhibiting crowd control and Shield of Durand is a charged stance whose taunt only lands on release. Galio facts verified at wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Galio and reused across this slice: Shield of Durand cuts magic 25/30/35/40/45% and physical exactly half (12.5/15/17.5/20/22.5%), passive magic shield 7.5/9/10.5/12/13.5% max health restoring after 12/10/8s untouched, taunt on release with radius 175-350 and 0.5-1.5s by channel time. Justice Punch knocks up 0.75s, cannot be interrupted mid-travel, disabled while Grounded, halts on terrain or champions. Winds of War 825, tornado 2s, no slow. Hero's Entrance channels 2.75s, CC-immune after 1.25s. Colossal Smash is a 5s empowered auto scaling with 60% bonus MR.
